tensions.poleA: Maintainers can't dismiss high uptime requirements
tensions.poleB: Businesses rely on unpaid open-source dependencies

tensions.toResolve: How can businesses secure critical dependencies if maintainers are not compensated for uptime?

stakeholders.name: Volunteer harvesters
stakeholders.role: facilitators recording post-session reflections on phones to surface festival themes
stakeholders.stake: capture honest attendee debate and display key insights on hallway screens without exposing anyone

stakeholders.name: Frontline activists
stakeholders.role: campaigners, student organisers, and digital rights defenders handling device seizures and takedown appeals
stakeholders.stake: protect movement participants from surveillance and recover seized accounts and hardware

stakeholders.name: Local archive keepers
stakeholders.role: oral historians, community radio archivists, and village librarians managing physical and local digital collections
stakeholders.stake: preserve collective stories and cultural records on their own timeline without losing community control

stakeholders.name: Open source maintainers
stakeholders.role: software engineers and model builders creating and maintaining shared libraries, standards, and model weights
stakeholders.stake: keep foundational tools running sustainably without burning out on unpaid labor

stakeholders.name: Festival artists
stakeholders.role: installation makers, musicians, illustrators, and textile practitioners exhibiting at the festival
stakeholders.stake: be credited and respected as the core argument rather than decorative fixtures or unconsented training data

stakeholders.name: Venture-backed founders
stakeholders.role: entrepreneurs building privacy-oriented consumer apps funded by equity investors
stakeholders.stake: keep payroll met and find viable business models without surrendering user data to investor growth targets

stakeholders.name: Community infrastructure operators
stakeholders.role: technicians and co-op founders running local mesh nodes, small hosting setups, and neighbourhood energy grids
stakeholders.stake: provide reliable local power, connectivity, and hosting governed directly by users rather than distant servers

relations.label: the phone on the table listening
relations.detail: Activists interrogate the recording pipeline and cloud jurisdiction while agreeing to keep speaking so their security warnings reach the wider event.

aspects.note: Activists insist on logging their explicit questions about recording security directly into the transcript.

relations.label: every archive is a target list
relations.detail: Activists point out that open model weights and published case files arm state surveillance units faster than they help frontline organisers.

aspects.note: Surveillance units apply publicly released open weights directly to transcripts of intercepted phone calls.

relations.label: the tool and the thief
relations.detail: Artists confront downstream developers and tool users over unconsented dataset scraping while creators absorb the public backlash for corporate scraping practices.

aspects.note: Downstream creators absorb direct hostility from peers while the companies responsible for scraping remain out of reach.

relations.label: running on unpaid attention
relations.detail: Funded tech startups build entire product architectures upon open-source libraries without contributing funding or knowing how to invoice maintainers.

aspects.note: Commercial privacy software risks immediate collapse if uncompensated library maintainers burn out.

relations.label: stopping at the tram line
relations.detail: Venture founders constrained by board growth mandates contrast their scale pressures against community co-ops deliberately bounding their geographic reach.

aspects.note: Community co-ops enforce strict geographic borders to protect member governance and avoid overexpansion.

relations.label: a server in the school cupboard
relations.detail: Community memory keepers rely on physical neighborhood servers and trusted caretakers to preserve local archives rather than renting corporate cloud infrastructure.

aspects.note: Village institutions maintain functional local backups through physical hardware and known community caretakers.

relations.label: asking before recording
relations.detail: Archivists and artists protect tactile and oral heritage by holding recordings private until elders and communities grant explicit consent.

aspects.note: Oral historians retain unshared community recordings in closed folders to honor elder boundaries against automated harvesting.
